title.value: Cut Across the Grain and Count the Years

description.value: A cautionary account attached to a named stretch of the eastern cuts, told by former company foremen and now by their households. It states what was done, in what order, and what the crust did about it, and it does not name anybody as being at fault.

content.value:
Cut with the grain and the crust carries you for a generation. Cut across it and the crust carries you for seven years, and the seventh is the good one.

The third channel was cut across the grain because the brine was better there and because the season was short. Everybody knew what it was. Nobody said it, and there is no dishonesty in that, because it was written on the floor for anyone to read.

In the seventh year the working floor rang differently underfoot in the morning and the same men went out on it in the afternoon. That is the part to remember. Not the cutting. The afternoon.

Two hundred metres away and I saw it go, and it did not sound like anything. Say that as well, when you tell it.

notes.value: Eleven versions have been collected and they agree closely except on the number of collapses, which runs from three to nine. The registered figure of five comes from the survey's own instrument record and appears in none of the accounts.
